newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse slides 1.2 pts in flat trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse slides 1.2 pts in flat trading.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were quiet in sluggish trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with several blue chips edging down, dragging the SAX index lower with them.
Bank VUB closed down five crowns at 1,680, while the investment fund VUB Kupon fell nine crowns to 631 as the SAX index eased 1.2 points to 186.38.
Overall volume fell to 181,558 shares from 218,640 on Wednesday, but only 800 changed hands on the BSE floor.
Brokers, however, said they remained positive, expecting low prices to attract more foreign investors and liquidity to increase over the next month.
"The market also lacks more fresh issues, which would help increase its liquidity," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
Steel maker VSZ lost one crown to close at 642, but brokers said the share has potential to increase in the near future.
"There is demand for VSZ shares at the current levels, but shareholders are not likely to accept such low prices and this should push the its price higher," Briska said.
Oil refiner Slovnaft and oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade at all.
Turnover rose to 87.46 million crowns from 67.66 million.
